Typography: Renders text with Voice tokens: family, size, weight, line height, and role.
Enforces Edenred Black for display/titles/numerals and Ubuntu for body/UI text.
Maps roles to semantic HTML and product copy hierarchy.
Handles captions, labels, body, display, numerals, and code without raw CSS.
Spacing: Lays out children with Frame token gaps.
Supports semantic gaps for component, subsection, section, and page rhythm.
Responds to density without per-component hacks.
Prevents arbitrary margins between child elements.
Iconography: Renders Material Symbols through the Symbol foundation.
Enforces semantic icon names and accessible-name rules.
Keeps icon size and color tokenized.
Shows missing icon states during development.
Density: Declares sm, md, or lg at the page or surface level.
Coordinates Spacing, Typography, Iconography, Focus, Loading, Disabled, and Breakpoints.
Gives components their scale defaults before variant, intent, and state are applied.
Prevents public component size overrides and local compact or comfortable hacks.
Surface: Owns structural backgrounds, section rhythm, panel framing, overlay body structure, and inline grouping.
Coordinates Color, Spacing, Radius, Elevation, Density, Focus, Breakpoints, Disabled, and State before child components render.
Lets theme and density cascade into composed components without pattern-local visual class roots.
Prevents Card from becoming a generic layout wrapper.
Field Action: Names local field-adjacent actions such as clear, reveal, picker, validate, recover, retry, and resend.
Defines target field relationship, pressed/loading/disabled state, focus policy, and message policy before choosing Button or Icon Button.
Coordinates Focus, Message, Disabled, Loading, Iconography, Spacing, Radius, and Measurement for field behavior.
Prevents fake buttons, raw icons, and duplicated picker or recovery behavior in demos and patterns.
fallback: Expose a small API that maps to foundations and token aliases.
Work across density, responsive, keyboard, touch, screen reader, contrast, and reduced-motion requirements when relevant.
Prevent raw visual values or duplicated implementation decisions.
